items.text: Theelectricmotoris one of the most importantuses of the motor effect. Figure 21.7shows the mostimportant featuresofa simple d.c.electricmotor.

items.label: text
items.text: When there is current in the loop of wire,one side ofit will experience a force pushing it upwards.The other side will feel a forcepushing it downwards,so the loop will begin to rotate （turn).

items.label: text
items.text: As the loop reaches the vertical position,itsmomentum takesitpast the vertical.lf therotationis to continue the forceson thewiresmustnow be reversedso that the wire at the top isnowpushed down and thebottomone is pushed up.

items.label: text
items.text: This canbe done easilyby using a split ring to connect theloop of wire to the electrical supply.Noweach time theloop ofwirepasses the vertical position,the connections change,the direction of the current changes,and the forceson the different sidesof theloop changedirection.The loop will rotate continuously.

items.label: text
items.text: Toincrease the rate atwhich themotor tums we can:

items.label: list_item
items.text: increase the number of turns orloops of wire,making a coil

items.label: list_item
items.text: increase the strength of the magneticfield

items.label: text
items.text: Althoughyou will notbe asked thisinyour examit isinteresting toknowhow commercial motors like the one used in thiselectricdrill differ from the simple motor described inFigure 21.7.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The permanent magnets are replaced with curved electromagnets capable of producingvery strongmagneticfields.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The single loop ofwire isreplacedwithseveral coilsofwirewrapped onthesame axis.This makes the motor more powerful and allows it to run more smoothly.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Thecoils are wrapped on a soft iron core that hasbeen coveredby a thin layer of plastic.Thismakes the motormore efficient and morepowerful.
